response.query: Which authentication, TLS/encryption, endpoint hardening, logging/retention, and breach-response timelines should be documented for webhooks ingesting Facebook content?
response.answer: Use HTTPS for webhook endpoints, implement mTLS for encryption, enforce strong authentication, maintain logs for at least one year, and set breach-response timelines within 24 hours.

results.content:
Title: Encryption and Authentication at the endpoint with WinMagic
In this blog I explain why it makes sense to use the same **endpoint security solution** for both encryption for data at rest on the device and authentication to servers and web services such as SaaS. So strong user authentication at pre-boot BEFORE the data is decrypted is important. As with encryption, there is also a need for key management and recovery for users that lose their authenticators (security key). If your organization needs both endpoint encryption and strong authentication, then security is obviously an important requirement. **Here is an example of a day in the life of a user with integrated Full Disk Encryption and Authentication where it all works together seamlessly:**. | **2.** User is prompted for pre-boot authentication BEFORE the OS is even loaded, for strong security. | **3.** User enters a short 6 digit PIN to unlock the computers security hardware (Just like when powering up an iPhone) Then, transparently, and automatically the drive encryption is cryptographically unlocked, the OS is decrypted as it is loaded into memory and the user is logged into their Windows account. | **4.** Users connects to Salesforce,  Enters their Salesforce password (Salesforce is 2nd  factor authentication)  Uses biometrics (e.g. finger print) as the 2nd authentication factor  or perhaps just touches a button to confirm user presence. Under the covers, one product orchestrates the strong cryptographic authentication and encryption that is occurring – totally transparent to the user. In the example above I am using a Salesforce password along with asymmetric crypto (a Security key) to authenticate. Rather it bypasses MFA by faking the session cookie or token that the server can store on the user’s endpoint device, thereby authorizing continued access after the initial  authentication is performed. It makes sense to use the same endpoint security solution for both encryption and authentication. results.title: Ingesting Webhooks From Stripe — The Better Way | by Superstream | Medium
results.content: # Ingesting Webhooks From Stripe — The Better Way. Learn what webhooks are, and how you use them with Stripe to react to events quickly and in real-time with greater reliability using a streaming platform. This post will show you everything you need to know about webhooks, including what they are, how they work, examples, and how they can be improved using Memphis. ## What are Webhooks? Webhooks stand out for their effectiveness for both the provider and the user. When the webhook initiates an HTTP request to your application, usually through a POST method, your task is to interpret and handle this incoming data effectively. ## The downsides of webhooks. Webhooks deliver or push events to your clients’ services, requiring them to handle the resulting back pressure. 2. **Implementing a server:**For your client’s services to receive webhooks, they need a server that listens to incoming events. While some triggered webhooks might lead to insignificant events, others can result in critical issues, such as incomplete datasets where orders fail to be documented in CRM or new shipping instructions are not being processed. 4. **Persistent:**Standard webhook systems generally lack event persistence for future audits and replays. While setting up an endpoint for users to retrieve past events is feasible, it demands meticulous handling, intricate business logic, an extra database, and increased complexity for the client. ## Why to use webhooks with Stripe. To get this real-time event flow, you’ll need to set up webhook endpoints in your application. Once you’ve registered these endpoints, Stripe becomes your real-time informant, pushing event data directly to your application’s webhook endpoint as things happen in your Stripe account. Webhook events are your go-to for monitoring asynchronous activities. ## Why use Memphis as your Stripe’s webhook destination. 1. Convert the push to pull: Memphis.dev operates as a pull-based message broker where clients actively pull and consume data from the broker. 4. Replay: The client has the flexibility to rotate the active offset, enabling easy access to read and replay any past event that complies with the retention policy and is still stored. 1. results.title: Hardening TLS for WLAN 802.1X Authentication – Frame by Frame
results.content: Microsoft published an update to Windows 7 and above to allow the use of TLS 1.1 and TLS 1.2 in its 802.1X supplicant, if configured manually for now. TLS 1.2 is the default TLS version used in the supplicants for Windows 10, ~~Mac OS 10.11, iOS 9~~, and Android 6.0 (Update: It appears that Apple has deferred their decision to default to TLS 1.2 in iOS 9/ Mac OS 10.11 until a later release). This frame includes the TLS version requested by the client along with its supported cipher suites. Next, the RADIUS server will respond with a “Server Hello” frame which specifies the TLS version and cipher suite to be used during the TLS session, and includes the server certificate as well. The server will choose the best cipher suite that both client and server support and the highest TLS version that both support as well. They are still on TLS 1.0.
